title: TOR in Germany: Knowledge and clinical decision-making among physicians – a vignette-based cross-sectional study
summary:
Background: When a person’s heart suddenly stops beating in hospital, an emergency team tries to bring them back to life. This does not always succeed. The doctors then have to decide whether and when to stop. Since 2025, there have been new recommendations from German medical societies and a decision rule developed in Scandinavia. How well resident physicians in Germany know these recommendations has not yet been studied.

Research question: How well do physicians know these rules? Is this knowledge related to their general knowledge of resuscitation and to their professional experience?

Methods: Physicians attending training courses in Arnsberg voluntarily answer an online questionnaire without giving their name. This takes about 15 to 20 minutes. The questionnaire contains fictitious patient cases, knowledge questions and questions about their professional background. The results are intended to help improve medical training in a targeted way.
conditions: In-hospital cardiac arrest; decision to terminate resuscitation (termination of resuscitation)
